Mark Baisley

Republican candidate for United States Senator, Colorado · Challenger

Colorado state senator; works in aerospace, defense and cybersecurity technology

Mark Baisley is a Republican Colorado state senator from Woodland Park. He served in the Colorado House before he was elected to the state Senate in 2022. He first ran for governor this cycle, switched to the U.S. Senate race in January 2026, and is the Republican nominee against incumbent Democrat John Hickenlooper.

Where Baisley stands

Health care / Medicaid
Supports the Medicaid work requirements in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. Says it is a success when someone leaves Medicaid and a failure when someone enrolls, and that he would have voted for the bill.
Health care
Supports Sen. Rick Scott's "More Affordable Care Act", which would send federal subsidies to consumers instead of insurers. Proposes tax-exempt health savings accounts for routine care, with insurance kept for catastrophic events.
Legal immigration
Says current legal immigration pathways are enough, and that they admit vetted people who have job skills, can support themselves and want to assimilate.
Immigration enforcement
Opposes letting people who are in the U.S. illegally stay. Supports letting federal authorities set up immigration detention facilities where they are needed.
Iran
Supports the Trump administration's military campaign against Iran. Says Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon and argues that higher fuel prices are a necessary cost of confronting terrorism.
Fuel prices
Supports temporarily suspending federal gas and diesel taxes. Supports the administration's deal to buy diesel from Russia, though he said he was uncomfortable relying on Russia.
Social Security
Proposes investment accounts for newborns modeled on Trump Accounts. Says about $3,000 invested at birth could grow to more than $1 million by age 65 and serve as an alternative to Social Security.
Fiscal policy / National debt
Wants to shrink the federal government. Says a smaller government is the way to grow the economy and recapture affordability.
Tariffs / Taxes
Supports tariffs and wants tariff revenue to eventually replace the federal income tax. Favors a flat income tax.
Trump administration
Says Colorado should work with President Trump more, rather than fight him at every step. Criticized the decision to move U.S. Space Command headquarters from Colorado to Alabama.

Background

  • Colorado state senator, 2023–present (elected 2022)
  • Colorado House of Representatives, 2019–2022
  • Ran for Colorado governor in the 2026 cycle; left that race in January 2026 to run for U.S. Senate
  • Works in technology, aerospace, defense and cybersecurity
  • Lives in Woodland Park, Colorado; age 71
